newsitem.title: UK: Celltech claws back some losses on results.
newsitem.headline: Celltech claws back some losses on results.

text.p: Shares in British biotechnology company Celltech Plc on Wednesday clawed back some of their recent severe losses after reporting clinical trial results and financial data in line with expectations.

Celltech, whose shares more than halved last week after its German partner Bayer AG said late-stage trials in the U.S. had shown that a joint drug for septic shock failed to prevent deaths, saw its stock open 8.5p stronger at 342.5p.

Dresdner Kleinwort Benson pharmaceutical analyst Jane Fisken said the share price fall last week had been "grossly overdone". "We're still about 45 percent off from where we were before the septic shock statement," she noted.

Analysts say the Celltech share price will be dragged back up amid positive data from trials and if the company announces new U.S. partners to help develop drugs for Crohn's disease and rheumatoid arthritis.

Celltech, which posted wider half-year, pre-tax losses of 5.9 million stg against 3.7 million last time, also said a European clinical study of its human antibody which could be used to treat asthma and other allergic diseases should start in the second half of 1997.
By 0850 GMT, the stock had jumped 18.5p, or 5.4 percent, to 352.5p.
